description:
## Why
Codex needs explicit lifecycle observations beyond Return and notify, but enabling c11’s adapter must not also grant trust to the operator’s unrelated hooks. Backlog item: J4.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Resources/bin/codex:222` prepends only the notify override; `:47` forwards the guarded legacy callback. `:160`–`:209` preserve exact runtime conversation ownership and must not regress.
- Upstream: `CLI/CMUXCLI+CodexFireAndForgetHooks.swift:181` says tenant/project/session hook layers append together, while `:220` injects --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust. This is a concrete trust-risk counterexample, not proof of isolation.
- Research: BACKLOG.md J4/D2; report 03 Lead’s hypothesis; report 01 Codex canary; Astra §6 D2. Reports cite Codex 0.159.3; the implementation must verify the version it actually supports.

## Scope
In: a reproducible trust-isolation probe, optional --enable hooks plus -c hooks.* adapter only if proven, session.started canary/degraded status, and notify fallback. Out: computed private trust hashes, persistent hooks/config installation, redirecting the operator home to hide settings, blanket trust bypass, answers, and broadening permission mode.

## Approach
First probe a disposable controlled profile with c11-owned hooks alongside untrusted tenant and project hooks. Compare execution with and without the bypass flag and inspect persistent writes. A successful c11 SessionStart alone is insufficient. If trust isolation is not proved, do not ship the bypass: keep notify and expose missing/degraded capability. If proved for the supported version, inject minimal optional observer hooks; preserve argv precedence, root identity and operator-selected configuration. Record a bounded launch canary deadline in the adapter contract.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The versioned probe demonstrates whether c11’s hooks run while untrusted tenant/project hooks remain untrusted and do not execute because of c11’s added flag. Record the actual counterexample or proof, not just a start event.
2. If that proof fails or is inconclusive, the shipped wrapper remains on notify, adds no bypass/trusted-hash workaround and reports its limited capability. If it passes, record the supported-version gate and actual lifecycle fixture coverage.
3. When session.started does not arrive within the declared deadline, the adapter reports degraded and preserves notify fallback; returning evidence is attributed to the current root session, not a prior launch.
4. The F3/GAF-13 child callback cannot finish the root, duplicate notify/hook completion is not counted twice, and wrapper launches/resumes preserve existing exact conversation behavior.
5. Controlled-profile before/after inspection shows no c11-caused tenant config or hook-trust writes; operator hooks/settings/permission mode remain in control. Socket failure does not hold the agent launch indefinitely.

## Validation
Run behavioral argv/fallback/canary tests, then the real installed Codex trust probe in a disposable fixture profile on Atlas. Never alter the operator’s live ~/.codex. Use the tagged socket for lifecycle observations and real UI smoke for marks, with verified display, timer and dismissal. Re-run version compatibility probes on supported Codex changes; F2 measures hook overhead. Passing fallback with a recorded failed isolation probe is an explicitly valid result.

## Dependencies
Depends on J2 and its source/ownership schema. F3 provides the root/child and interruption fixtures. J5 supplies advisory transcript observations independently. J8 must document actual supported/degraded coverage.
Within-workstream prerequisites: J2 (C11-273).

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.
title: Gate Codex per-process lifecycle hooks on isolated trust proof
